Lesson pages retain a consistent **“Check your understanding”** component: a small number of focused questions with collapsed answers. These are intended for immediate retrieval and conceptual reinforcement. This catalogue is the entry point for **extended exercises**: calculations, multi-step problems, diagnosis, implementation-oriented reasoning, and transfer tasks. The substantial exercise sets live on their own topic pages so that they can grow without turning this page into a long, flat worksheet.

## How to use this space

- Start with the preparation listed in the relevant collection; follow other references only when needed.
- Attempt each task before opening its solution. State assumptions and identify conditions under which your answer would fail.
- Use transfer prompts to test whether the reasoning generalizes beyond the worked example.
- Solutions are collapsed by default. A correct result without reasoning is not sufficient evidence of mastery.

## Planned collections

The following topics are part of the longer-term practice curriculum. They are not presented as published collections until their exercises are available.

| Collection | Planned focus | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Pretraining | Training curves, validation loss, perplexity, checkpoints, and reproducibility | Planned |
| Fine-tuning | Classification, SFT, target alignment, loss masking, data quality, and overfitting | Planned |
| Evaluation | Baselines, metrics, contamination, uncertainty, and error analysis | One standalone transfer exercise is available in [Experimental evaluation](experimental-evaluation.qmd); a broader collection remains to be built. |
| Efficiency | LoRA/QLoRA, memory estimates, cost, and trade-offs | Planned |
| Advanced topics | DPO, attention variants, critical reading, and experimental design | Planned |

## A note on lesson self-checks

Do not move every question out of a lesson. A short, tightly scoped self-check belongs beside the concept it reinforces. Move an exercise here when it requires sustained calculation, several reasoning steps, a worked solution, comparison of alternatives, or transfer beyond the immediate lesson. The dedicated collections may link back to lesson pages for preparation, but should not duplicate their conceptual explanations.
